newsitem.title: USA: PG&E completes Valero Energy acquisition.
newsitem.headline: PG&E completes Valero Energy acquisition.

text.p: PG&E Corp on Thursday closed its $1.5 billion acquisition of Valero Energy Corp's natural gas business, the latest strategic move in its bid to become a leading U.S. and international energy provider.
The transaction includes the spin-off of Valero's wholly-owned subsidiary, Valero Refining and Marketing Co, as an independent publicly traded company.

In the deal, PG&E acquired more than 8,000 miles of natural gas and gas liquids pipelines, eight gas processing plants and about 13 billion cubic feet of natural gas storage for stock and debt assumption.
"The real message here is that PG&E has really come on the scene," said Lyn Maddox, who heads up PG&E's Houston-based energy trading operations.

Robert Glynn, Jr., PG&E's chief executive officer, said in a statement, "This acquisition is a key part of our plan to have an asset base as well as a trading and retail presence in each major region that we serve."
PG&E has been pushing to boost its domestic electric wholesale volumes as the San Francisco-based utility holding company positions itself to compete in deregulated retail electric markets.
The company had trading volumes of 3.1 gigawatts in the first quarter and projected volumes of 10-12 gigawatts for the year, Maddox said in a recent interview.

As PG&E expands into selected domestic retail markets, analysts expect the company to compete first in markets where it already controls generating assets, including the East Coast, northeast and southeast.
"We're going to focus regionally and market research is going to point us in the right direction," PG&E's Steve Reynolds said.
Over the next two years, PG&E has budgeted $100 million to develop the infrastructure for its retail push, installing information and billing systems and marketing its brand name.

PG&E Energy Services today said it acquired Utility Service Associates, a Columbia, S.C.-based utility billing services company that analyzes utility rates and provides other energy services to U.S.-based Fortune 500 customers.

PG&E's gas transmission business, one of the company's five core operations, is operating near its 2 billion cubic feet per day capacity. The company plans to expand volumes it handles through off-system trades, Maddox said.
"On-system volumes can't increase because we are substantially full," he said.

PG&E's Pacific Gas & Electric Co has 13 million customers in northern and central California, and its US Generating Co. is the nation's second-largest independent power producer with 17 plants and 3,400 megawatts of generating capacity.
The company expects to more than double that capacity in the next five years through acquisitions and development.

The Valero deal follows a 1996 acquisition of Corpus Christi, Texas-based Teco Pipeline Co. Consolidating the companies' operations leaves PG&E as the 5th largest U.S. natural gas and 14th largest electric trader, it said.
"The people, the systems are in place," Reynolds said, adding that the company will look at "bite-sized" acquisitions to fill out its gas transmission system in resource basins.
